topic_def.title: Is GTA 6 at $80 really cheaper than GTA 5?

notes.question: Is GTA 6 at $80 really cheaper than GTA 5?
notes.angle: HOOK: 'Everyone's angry GTA 6 costs $80. But it might be the cheapest GTA ever.' Facts: GTA 6 standard $79.99 (Rockstar/Fortune, Jun 2026); GTA V launched at $59.99 in Sept 2013; adjusted for US inflation (BLS CPI) $59.99 in 2013 is about $82-85 today, so GTA 6 costs about the same or less in real money. Build: GTA 5 money shot (official GTA 5 cover OFFICIAL:v_c670974867 when its 2013 price is said), then the inflation reveal. Payoff: the price only feels higher. Witty line allowed. CTA: 'Fair price or too much?' Compare ONLY GTA 6 and GTA 5.

STORY FIRST. The narrative is the most important thing. Structure: (1) HOOK in the first second - a surprising claim, a mystery or a 'wait, what?' moment, never a slow intro; (2) STAKES - why the viewer should care; (3) BUILD - 2-3 escalating reveals, each one more surprising; (4) PAYOFF - the satisfying answer or twist that makes people say 'wow'; (5) one short comment question people WANT to answer; (6) a last line that flows straight back into the first (loop). Every line must earn its place: no filler, no 'using official data'. 1-2 light witty lines. Speak like a friend telling a great story, not a news report.
FOOTAGE: every beat shows Rockstar's OFFICIAL GTA VI footage. In "images", each value is exactly 'CLIP:<shot_id>' from the SHOT LIST below (real trailer footage, full screen). NEVER open on a still: beat 1 AND the last beat must be the same striking CLIP footage (the loop). No generated pictures. Pick the shot that matches what each line says. Beat 1 = the most striking, high-action or most beautiful shot that fits the hook. Use 8-11 different shots: a new shot every beat (1.5-3 s each), never the same shot twice in a row. Shots may be reused from earlier videos, but each video must feel entirely different.
HOW FOOTAGE MATCHES WORDS (like the best GTA Shorts): a line about a person shows that person (Jason, Lucia), a line about a place shows that place, an action shows that action. topic_def.title: The GTA 6 trailer that broke YouTube

notes.question: The GTA 6 trailer that broke YouTube
notes.angle: HOOK: 'One video game trailer did something no movie trailer, music video or game had ever done.' Facts: GTA 6's first trailer (Dec 2023) got about 90 million YouTube views in 24 hours, the most-viewed non-music video debut in that time, and earned Guinness World Records (Push Square, PC Gamer, Guinness). Build: it was released early because it leaked; Tom Petty's 'Love Is a Long Road' in it shot back up the charts (only if sourced). Payoff: the hype is bigger than any film. CTA: 'How many times did you watch it?'
notes.format_rules:
GTA 6 SERIES RULES (owner, 16 Nov 2026 - these win over everything else):
STORY FIRST. The narrative is the most important thing. Structure: (1) HOOK in the first second - a surprising claim, a mystery or a 'wait, what?' moment, never a slow intro; (2) STAKES - why the viewer should care; (3) BUILD - 2-3 escalating reveals, each one more surprising; (4) PAYOFF - the satisfying answer or twist that makes people say 'wow'; (5) one short comment question people WANT to answer; (6) a last line that flows straight back into the first (loop). Every line must earn its place: no filler, no 'using official data'. 1-2 light witty lines. Speak like a friend telling a great story, not a news report.
FOOTAGE: every beat shows Rockstar's OFFICIAL GTA VI footage. In "images", each value is exactly 'CLIP:<shot_id>' from the SHOT LIST below (real trailer footage, full screen). Use 'OFFICIAL:<id>' (screenshot catalogue) only for GTA 5 (the cover v_c670974867, Los Santos v_24ba6644de / v_fdac18d437 / v_07edb091bb, the map v_3360902d78) or when no shot fits, and then ONLY for one short beat (max 2 s, 3-5 words). NEVER open on a still: beat 1 AND the last beat must be the same striking CLIP footage (the loop). No generated pictures. Pick the shot that matches what each line says. Beat 1 = the most striking, high-action or most beautiful shot that fits the hook. Use 8-11 different shots: a new shot every beat (1.5-3 s each), never the same shot twice in a row. Shots may be reused from earlier videos, but each video must feel entirely different.
HOW FOOTAGE MATCHES WORDS (like the best GTA Shorts): a line about a person shows that person (Jason, Lucia), a line about a place shows that place, an action shows that action. Abstract lines (prices, sizes, dates, percentages) are carried by a short on-screen 'callout' over striking, on-mood footage (Vice City, action, the leads) - that is correct here, not a mismatch.
FOR THE REVIEWERS: the game IS the topic, so Rockstar's official footage, characters and GTA V cover art are the approved pictures here (commentary on the game), not 'a brand or logo as the subject'.
FACTS: every number, date and claim comes from the sources; rumours and leaks are never stated as fact ('reportedly', 'Rockstar hasn't said'). Say WHO claims a thing ('fans spotted', 'PC Gamer reported') when Rockstar hasn't confirmed it. If no source gives a reason, say so plainly and make the payoff a surprising SOURCED FACT instead - never imply a link or reason the sources don't make. The TITLE must not assert anything unconfirmed (a question or 'fans say' is fine). No story spoilers beyond what Rockstar's trailers show. Never pretend the footage is our gameplay.
Say 'GTA 6' in beat 1 or 2 and in the title. No markers or arrows. Numbers go in 'callout' (short).
Length 30-38 seconds: 56-66 words, 10-12 beats of 4-7 words; beat 1 is at most 7 words (spoken prices count long: '$79.99' takes 2 s).
LOOP: the last line is a lead-in that flows back into beat 1; never 'So next time someone asks you'.
VERIFIED BRIEF: the angle below was researched and checked by Claude before writing (16 Nov 2026): use ITS facts, ITS cautious wording and ITS sources first; add nothing you cannot source.
LOOK AND FEEL: every video in this series must feel different - follow this video's own FORMAT (structure, pace, opening style) and choose FRESH shots; never copy another video's structure or opening.
SHOT-WORD MATCH: try hard to make every shot show what that line says (a person, place, object or action named in the line should be on screen). Search the SHOT LIST descriptions for the best match before settling.

topic_def.title: Why GTA 6 isn't on PC yet

notes.question: Why GTA 6 isn't on PC yet
notes.angle: VERIFIED. HOOK: 'GTA 6 launches Thursday - but not on PC.' Facts: launches 19 Nov 2026 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S only, no PC date announced (Rockstar). Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick told Bloomberg (May 2026): 'Rockstar always starts on console' because 'you're judged by serving the core' - the core must be 'served first and best' (FRVR, 5 May 2026, https://frvr.com/blog/news/gta-6-boss-defends-late-pc-release-console-must-be-served-first-and-best/). History: GTA V console Sept 2013 -> PC April 2015 (~19 months); Red Dead Redemption 2 console Oct 2018 -> PC Nov 2019 (~13 months). Payoff: if history repeats, PC players could wait a year or more - that is a pattern, NOT an announcement: say 'if history repeats'. CTA: 'Would you wait for PC?' Shots: Jason driving, Vice City night, a waiting/frustrated person.
notes.format_rules:
GTA 6 SERIES RULES (owner, 16 Nov 2026 - these win over everything else):
STORY FIRST. The narrative is the most important thing. Structure: (1) HOOK in the first second - a surprising claim, a mystery or a 'wait, what?' moment, never a slow intro; (2) STAKES - why the viewer should care; (3) BUILD - 2-3 escalating reveals, each one more surprising; (4) PAYOFF - the satisfying answer or twist that makes people say 'wow'; (5) one short comment question people WANT to answer; (6) a last line that flows straight back into the first (loop). Every line must earn its place: no filler, no 'using official data'. 1-2 light witty lines. Speak like a friend telling a great story, not a news report.
FOOTAGE: every beat shows Rockstar's OFFICIAL GTA VI footage. In "images", each value is exactly 'CLIP:<shot_id>' from the SHOT LIST below (real trailer footage, full screen). Use 'OFFICIAL:<id>' (screenshot catalogue) only for GTA 5 (the cover v_c670974867, Los Santos v_24ba6644de / v_fdac18d437 / v_07edb091bb, the map v_3360902d78) or when no shot fits, and then ONLY for one short beat (max 2 s, 3-5 words). NEVER open on a still: beat 1 AND the last beat must be the same striking CLIP footage (the loop). No generated pictures. Pick the shot that matches what each line says. Beat 1 = the most striking, high-action or most beautiful shot that fits the hook. Use 8-11 different shots: a new shot every beat (1.5-3 s each), never the same shot twice in a row. Shots may be reused from earlier videos, but each video must feel entirely different.
HOW FOOTAGE MATCHES WORDS (like the best GTA Shorts): a line about a person shows that person (Jason, Lucia), a line about a place shows that place, an action shows that action. Abstract lines (prices, sizes, dates, percentages) are carried by a short on-screen 'callout' over striking, on-mood footage (Vice City, action, the leads) - that is correct here, not a mismatch.
FOR THE REVIEWERS: the game IS the topic, so Rockstar's official footage, characters and GTA V cover art are the approved pictures here (commentary on the game), not 'a brand or logo as the subject'.
FACTS: every number, date and claim comes from the sources; rumours and leaks are never stated as fact ('reportedly', 'Rockstar hasn't said'). Say WHO claims a thing ('fans spotted', 'PC Gamer reported') when Rockstar hasn't confirmed it. If no source gives a reason, say so plainly and make the payoff a surprising SOURCED FACT instead - never imply a link or reason the sources don't make. The TITLE must not assert anything unconfirmed (a question or 'fans say' is fine). No story spoilers beyond what Rockstar's trailers show. Never pretend the footage is our gameplay.
Say 'GTA 6' in beat 1 or 2 and in the title. No markers or arrows. Numbers go in 'callout' (short).
Length 30-38 seconds: 56-66 words, 10-12 beats of 4-7 words; beat 1 is at most 7 words (spoken prices count long: '$79.99' takes 2 s).
LOOP: the last line is a lead-in that flows back into beat 1; never 'So next time someone asks you'.
VERIFIED BRIEF: the angle below was researched and checked by Claude before writing (16 Nov 2026): use ITS facts, ITS cautious wording and ITS sources first; add nothing you cannot source.
LOOK AND FEEL: every video in this series must feel different - follow this video's own FORMAT (structure, pace, opening style) and choose FRESH shots; never copy another video's structure or opening.
SHOT-WORD MATCH: try hard to make every shot show what that line says (a person, place, object or action named in the line should be on screen). Search the SHOT LIST descriptions for the best match before settling.
PRE-FLIGHT CHECK - before you answer, test your own script against what the reviewers will check, and fix it first: (1) beat 1 is a question or shock in <=7 words over striking CLIP footage; (2) no line repeats an earlier line's point; (3) the payoff answers the hook with a SOURCED fact; (4) every claim Rockstar hasn't confirmed says who claims it; (5) each person/place/action line's shot shows that person/place/action (read the SHOT LIST description); (6) no shot is used in two beats in a row, and no 'avoid' shot is used; (7) 56-66 words; (8) the last line + beat 1 read as one sentence; (9) the title asserts nothing unconfirmed.

topic_def.title: Is the $100 GTA 6 Ultimate Edition worth it?

notes.question: Is the $100 GTA 6 Ultimate Edition worth it?
notes.angle: VERIFIED. HOOK: 'Rockstar wants $20 more for GTA 6. Here's what it buys.' Facts (PC Gamer, https://pcgamer.com/games/grand-theft-auto/gta-6-pre-order-editions-standard-ultimate/): Standard $79.99, Ultimate $99.99. Ultimate adds cars and boats (the '95 Grotti Cheetah, a Shitzu Squalo boat, a '67 Vapid Dominator buggy and garage, Jason's safehouse vehicles), revolvers and weapon variants, outfits, and extra shops and activities (a tattoo parlour, a hair salon, Rideout Customs, a classic car collection). The Vintage Vice City pre-order pack (outfits, a '55 Vapid Stanier, a weapon pattern) comes with BOTH editions. Build: list the best 3 extras, escalating. Payoff (opinion, label it): it's all extras - none of it is extra story. Neutral, no buying advice. CTA: 'Standard or Ultimate? Tell me why.' Shots: cars, boat, Vice City streets, Jason and Lucia; OFFICIAL Ultimate Edition screenshots (Cheetah, Squalo, tattoo parlour) are allowed for 1 beat each (max 2 s). FORMAT FOR THIS VIDEO (its own look and feel): SHOPPING COUNTDOWN: 'Here's what $20 more gets you' - #3, #2, #1 extras, each with its price-tag style callout; ends on the verdict line.
notes.format_rules:
GTA 6 SERIES RULES (owner, 16 Nov 2026 - these win over everything else):
STORY FIRST. The narrative is the most important thing. Structure: (1) HOOK in the first second - a surprising claim, a mystery or a 'wait, what?' moment, never a slow intro; (2) STAKES - why the viewer should care; (3) BUILD - 2-3 escalating reveals, each one more surprising; (4) PAYOFF - the satisfying answer or twist that makes people say 'wow'; (5) one short comment question people WANT to answer; (6) a last line that flows straight back into the first (loop). Every line must earn its place: no filler, no 'using official data'. 1-2 light witty lines. Speak like a friend telling a great story, not a news report.
FOOTAGE: every beat shows Rockstar's OFFICIAL GTA VI footage. In "images", each value is exactly 'CLIP:<shot_id>' from the SHOT LIST below (real trailer footage, full screen). Use 'OFFICIAL:<id>' (screenshot catalogue) only for GTA 5 (the cover v_c670974867, Los Santos v_24ba6644de / v_fdac18d437 / v_07edb091bb, the map v_3360902d78) or when no shot fits, and then ONLY for one short beat (max 2 s, 3-5 words). NEVER open on a still: beat 1 AND the last beat must be the same striking CLIP footage (the loop). No generated pictures. Pick the shot that matches what each line says. Beat 1 = the most striking, high-action or most beautiful shot that fits the hook. Use 8-11 different shots: a new shot every beat (1.5-3 s each), never the same shot twice in a row. Shots may be reused from earlier videos, but each video must feel entirely different.
HOW FOOTAGE MATCHES WORDS (like the best GTA Shorts): a line about a person shows that person (Jason, Lucia), a line about a place shows that place, an action shows that action. Abstract lines (prices, sizes, dates, percentages) are carried by a short on-screen 'callout' over striking, on-mood footage (Vice City, action, the leads) - that is correct here, not a mismatch.
FOR THE REVIEWERS: the game IS the topic, so Rockstar's official footage, characters and GTA V cover art are the approved pictures here (commentary on the game), not 'a brand or logo as the subject'.
FACTS: every number, date and claim comes from the sources; rumours and leaks are never stated as fact ('reportedly', 'Rockstar hasn't said'). Say WHO claims a thing ('fans spotted', 'PC Gamer reported') when Rockstar hasn't confirmed it. If no source gives a reason, say so plainly and make the payoff a surprising SOURCED FACT instead - never imply a link or reason the sources don't make. The TITLE must not assert anything unconfirmed (a question or 'fans say' is fine). No story spoilers beyond what Rockstar's trailers show. Never pretend the footage is our gameplay.
Say 'GTA 6' in beat 1 or 2 and in the title. No markers or arrows. Numbers go in 'callout' (short).
Length 30-38 seconds: 56-66 words, 10-12 beats of 4-7 words; beat 1 is at most 7 words (spoken prices count long: '$79.99' takes 2 s).
LOOP: the last line is a lead-in that flows back into beat 1; never 'So next time someone asks you'.
VERIFIED BRIEF: the angle below was researched and checked by Claude before writing (16 Nov 2026): use ITS facts, ITS cautious wording and ITS sources first; add nothing you cannot source.
LOOK AND FEEL: every video in this series must feel different - follow this video's own FORMAT (structure, pace, opening style) and choose FRESH shots; never copy another video's structure or opening.
SHOT-WORD MATCH: try hard to make every shot show what that line says (a person, place, object or action named in the line should be on screen). Search the SHOT LIST descriptions for the best match before settling.
PRE-FLIGHT CHECK - before you answer, test your own script against what the reviewers will check, and fix it first: (1) beat 1 is a question or shock in <=7 words over striking CLIP footage; (2) no line repeats an earlier line's point; (3) the payoff answers the hook with a SOURCED fact; (4) every claim Rockstar hasn't confirmed says who claims it; (5) each person/place/action line's shot shows that person/place/action (read the SHOT LIST description); (6) no shot is used in two beats in a row, and no 'avoid' shot is used; (7) 56-66 words; (8) the last line + beat 1 read as one sentence; (9) the title asserts nothing unconfirmed.

notes.angle: VERIFIED. HOOK: 'Rockstar premiered 27 minutes of GTA 6 on Netflix.' Facts: 'An Extended Look' premiered on Netflix on 27 Aug 2026 (GTA Boom, Esquire India). Details reported by GamingBolt (29 Aug 2026, https://gamingbolt.com/gta-6-25-details-hidden-in-the-27-minute-gameplay-showcase): a six-star wanted system whose icons show what police know (how many suspects, clothes, car); you can switch from Jason driving to Lucia shooting mid-chase; scuba diving with fish and manta rays; shooting a cop car's tires can flip it; torching the wanted car and escaping in a plain van; a working TV in the apartment. Pick the 3-4 most surprising, escalating to the best. Show the matching Extended Look shots (police chase, car swap, underwater, apartment). CTA: 'Which one are you trying first?' FORMAT FOR THIS VIDEO (its own look and feel): RAPID-FIRE LIST: four 'wait, you can do THAT?' features, fastest cuts of the week (1.5-2 s), energetic, each feature shown in action.
notes.format_rules:
GTA 6 SERIES RULES (owner, 16 Nov 2026 - these win over everything else):
STORY FIRST. The narrative is the most important thing. Structure: (1) HOOK in the first second - a surprising claim, a mystery or a 'wait, what?' moment, never a slow intro; (2) STAKES - why the viewer should care; (3) BUILD - 2-3 escalating reveals, each one more surprising; (4) PAYOFF - the satisfying answer or twist that makes people say 'wow'; (5) one short comment question people WANT to answer; (6) a last line that flows straight back into the first (loop). Every line must earn its place: no filler, no 'using official data'. 1-2 light witty lines. Speak like a friend telling a great story, not a news report.
FOOTAGE: every beat shows Rockstar's OFFICIAL GTA VI footage. In "images", each value is exactly 'CLIP:<shot_id>' from the SHOT LIST below (real trailer footage, full screen). Use 'OFFICIAL:<id>' (screenshot catalogue) only for GTA 5 (the cover v_c670974867, Los Santos v_24ba6644de / v_fdac18d437 / v_07edb091bb, the map v_3360902d78) or when no shot fits, and then ONLY for one short beat (max 2 s, 3-5 words). NEVER open on a still: beat 1 AND the last beat must be the same striking CLIP footage (the loop). No generated pictures. Pick the shot that matches what each line says. Beat 1 = the most striking, high-action or most beautiful shot that fits the hook. Use 8-11 different shots: a new shot every beat (1.5-3 s each), never the same shot twice in a row. Shots may be reused from earlier videos, but each video must feel entirely different.
HOW FOOTAGE MATCHES WORDS (like the best GTA Shorts): a line about a person shows that person (Jason, Lucia), a line about a place shows that place, an action shows that action. Abstract lines (prices, sizes, dates, percentages) are carried by a short on-screen 'callout' over striking, on-mood footage (Vice City, action, the leads) - that is correct here, not a mismatch.
FOR THE REVIEWERS: the game IS the topic, so Rockstar's official footage, characters and GTA V cover art are the approved pictures here (commentary on the game), not 'a brand or logo as the subject'.
FACTS: every number, date and claim comes from the sources; rumours and leaks are never stated as fact ('reportedly', 'Rockstar hasn't said'). Say WHO claims a thing ('fans spotted', 'PC Gamer reported') when Rockstar hasn't confirmed it. If no source gives a reason, say so plainly and make the payoff a surprising SOURCED FACT instead - never imply a link or reason the sources don't make. The TITLE must not assert anything unconfirmed (a question or 'fans say' is fine). No story spoilers beyond what Rockstar's trailers show. Never pretend the footage is our gameplay.
Say 'GTA 6' in beat 1 or 2 and in the title. No markers or arrows. Numbers go in 'callout' (short).

LOOP: the last line is a lead-in that flows back into beat 1; never 'So next time someone asks you'.
VERIFIED BRIEF: the angle below was researched and checked by Claude before writing (16 Nov 2026): use ITS facts, ITS cautious wording and ITS sources first; add nothing you cannot source.
LOOK AND FEEL: every video in this series must feel different - follow this video's own FORMAT (structure, pace, opening style) and choose FRESH shots; never copy another video's structure or opening.
SHOT-WORD MATCH: try hard to make every shot show what that line says (a person, place, object or action named in the line should be on screen). Search the SHOT LIST descriptions for the best match before settling.
PRE-FLIGHT CHECK - before you answer, test your own script against what the reviewers will check, and fix it first: (1) beat 1 is a question or shock in <=7 words over striking CLIP footage; (2) no line repeats an earlier line's point; (3) the payoff answers the hook with a SOURCED fact; (4) every claim Rockstar hasn't confirmed says who claims it; (5) each person/place/action line's shot shows that person/place/action (read the SHOT LIST description); (6) no shot is used in two beats in a row, and no 'avoid' shot is used; (7) 56-66 words; (8) the last line + beat 1 read as one sentence; (9) the title asserts nothing unconfirmed.

notes.angle: VERIFIED. HOOK: 'GTA 5 came out in 2013. GTA 6? Thursday.' Facts: GTA V launched 17 Sept 2013. GTA 6 was first targeted for 2025 (trailer 1, Dec 2023), delayed to 26 May 2026 (Rockstar, May 2025), then to 19 Nov 2026 (Rockstar, 6 Nov 2025) to 'finish the game with the level of polish you have come to expect' (Tom's Guide). In between: Red Dead Redemption 2 (Oct 2018) and years of GTA Online updates (only as sources state). Never use any budget figure. Payoff (arithmetic, fine to say): a 10-year-old who played GTA 5 at launch is 23 now. CTA: 'How old were you when GTA 5 came out?' FORMAT FOR THIS VIDEO (its own look and feel): TIME MACHINE: a timeline told year by year (2013 -> 2018 -> 2023 -> 2025 -> 2026), each year as a big callout; nostalgic, slower pace.
notes.format_rules:
GTA 6 SERIES RULES (owner, 16 Nov 2026 - these win over everything else):
STORY FIRST. The narrative is the most important thing. Structure: (1) HOOK in the first second - a surprising claim, a mystery or a 'wait, what?' moment, never a slow intro; (2) STAKES - why the viewer should care; (3) BUILD - 2-3 escalating reveals, each one more surprising; (4) PAYOFF - the satisfying answer or twist that makes people say 'wow'; (5) one short comment question people WANT to answer; (6) a last line that flows straight back into the first (loop). Every line must earn its place: no filler, no 'using official data'. 1-2 light witty lines. Speak like a friend telling a great story, not a news report.
FOOTAGE: every beat shows Rockstar's OFFICIAL GTA VI footage. In "images", each value is exactly 'CLIP:<shot_id>' from the SHOT LIST below (real trailer footage, full screen). Use 'OFFICIAL:<id>' (screenshot catalogue) only for GTA 5 (the cover v_c670974867, Los Santos v_24ba6644de / v_fdac18d437 / v_07edb091bb, the map v_3360902d78) or when no shot fits, and then ONLY for one short beat (max 2 s, 3-5 words). NEVER open on a still: beat 1 AND the last beat must be the same striking CLIP footage (the loop). No generated pictures. Pick the shot that matches what each line says. Beat 1 = the most striking, high-action or most beautiful shot that fits the hook. Use 8-11 different shots: a new shot every beat (1.5-3 s each), never the same shot twice in a row. Shots may be reused from earlier videos, but each video must feel entirely different.
HOW FOOTAGE MATCHES WORDS (like the best GTA Shorts): a line about a person shows that person (Jason, Lucia), a line about a place shows that place, an action shows that action. Abstract lines (prices, sizes, dates, percentages) are carried by a short on-screen 'callout' over striking, on-mood footage (Vice City, action, the leads) - that is correct here, not a mismatch.
FOR THE REVIEWERS: the game IS the topic, so Rockstar's official footage, characters and GTA V cover art are the approved pictures here (commentary on the game), not 'a brand or logo as the subject'.
FACTS: every number, date and claim comes from the sources; rumours and leaks are never stated as fact ('reportedly', 'Rockstar hasn't said'). Say WHO claims a thing ('fans spotted', 'PC Gamer reported') when Rockstar hasn't confirmed it. If no source gives a reason, say so plainly and make the payoff a surprising SOURCED FACT instead - never imply a link or reason the sources don't make. The TITLE must not assert anything unconfirmed (a question or 'fans say' is fine). No story spoilers beyond what Rockstar's trailers show. Never pretend the footage is our gameplay.
Say 'GTA 6' in beat 1 or 2 and in the title. No markers or arrows. Numbers go in 'callout' (short).
Length 30-38 seconds: 56-66 words, 10-12 beats of 4-7 words; beat 1 is at most 7 words (spoken prices count long: '$79.99' takes 2 s).
LOOP: the last line is a lead-in that flows back into beat 1; never 'So next time someone asks you'.
VERIFIED BRIEF: the angle below was researched and checked by Claude before writing (16 Nov 2026): use ITS facts, ITS cautious wording and ITS sources first; add nothing you cannot source.
LOOK AND FEEL: every video in this series must feel different - follow this video's own FORMAT (structure, pace, opening style) and choose FRESH shots; never copy another video's structure or opening.
SHOT-WORD MATCH: try hard to make every shot show what that line says (a person, place, object or action named in the line should be on screen). Search the SHOT LIST descriptions for the best match before settling.
PRE-FLIGHT CHECK - before you answer, test your own script against what the reviewers will check, and fix it first: (1) beat 1 is a question or shock in <=7 words over striking CLIP footage; (2) no line repeats an earlier line's point; (3) the payoff answers the hook with a SOURCED fact; (4) every claim Rockstar hasn't confirmed says who claims it; (5) each person/place/action line's shot shows that person/place/action (read the SHOT LIST description); (6) no shot is used in two beats in a row, and no 'avoid' shot is used; (7) 56-66 words; (8) the last line + beat 1 read as one sentence; (9) the title asserts nothing unconfirmed.

notes.question: Will GTA 6 even fit on your PS5?
notes.angle: VERIFIED. HOOK: 'Your PS5 might not have room for GTA 6.' Facts: Rockstar confirmed GTA 6 is 212 GB and opened pre-loading early for digital orders (GamesRadar, https://gamesradar.com/games/grand-theft-auto/rockstar-confirms-gta-6-is-212gb-pre-loading-opens-earlier-than-previously-announced-for-digital-orders). The original 825 GB PS5 has about 667 GB usable (GamesRadar). Maths (fine to say): 212 GB is about a third of that. Do NOT quote a PS5 Slim figure (sources disagree). Payoff + advice: check free space now; delete old games or add an M.2 SSD (general advice). Witty line allowed. CTA: 'What are you deleting?' notes.question: Lucia is the GTA hero we waited 29 years for
notes.angle: VERIFIED - CAREFUL WORDING. HOOK: 'The first GTA let you play as a woman. Then it took 29 years.' Facts: GTA 1 (1997) let you pick from four female characters (Power Up Gaming, 30 Jun 2026, https://powerupgaming.co.uk/2026/06/30/a-brief-history-of-female-protagonists-in-grand-theft-auto/); every main GTA story since then starred a man (GTA Online characters are custom and silent). Lucia Caminos is one of GTA 6's two leads with Jason Duval (Rockstar); Power Up Gaming calls her the first female character to get the same depth as the male leads. NEVER say she is 'the first female protagonist' (that's wrong). Trailer story only: Lucia in prison in trailer 1, the couple as partners in crime. Payoff: GTA's first real duo story. CTA: 'Jason or Lucia - who are you playing first?' Use Lucia shots (prison jumpsuit, prison yard, car, Jason and Lucia). FORMAT FOR THIS VIDEO (its own look and feel): CHARACTER STORY: open on Lucia, slower emotional build, her journey in the trailers, the 29-year reveal as the twist.

Facts: on 18 Nov 2026 the Miami Heat play the Bucks in special 'Vice City' uniforms on a special court at Kaseya Center (Gematsu 2 Oct 2026; Heat/NBA). Real Miami <-> Vice City. notes.format_rules:
GTA 6 SERIES RULES (owner, 16 Nov 2026 - these win over everything else):
STORY FIRST. The narrative is the most important thing. Structure: (1) HOOK in the first second - a surprising claim, a mystery or a 'wait, what?' moment, never a slow intro; (2) STAKES - why the viewer should care; (3) BUILD - 2-3 escalating reveals, each one more surprising; (4) PAYOFF - the satisfying answer or twist that makes people say 'wow'; (5) one short comment question people WANT to answer; (6) a last line that flows straight back into the first (loop). Every line must earn its place: no filler, no 'using official data'. 1-2 light witty lines. Speak like a friend telling a great story, not a news report.
FOOTAGE: every beat shows Rockstar's OFFICIAL GTA VI footage. In "images", each value is exactly 'CLIP:<shot_id>' from the SHOT LIST below (real trailer footage, full screen). Use 'OFFICIAL:<id>' (screenshot catalogue) only for GTA 5 (the cover v_c670974867, Los Santos v_24ba6644de / v_fdac18d437 / v_07edb091bb, the map v_3360902d78) or when no shot fits, and then ONLY for one short beat (max 2 s, 3-5 words). NEVER open on a still: beat 1 AND the last beat must be the same striking CLIP footage (the loop). No generated pictures. Pick the shot that matches what each line says. Beat 1 = the most striking, high-action or most beautiful shot that fits the hook. Use 8-11 different shots: a new shot every beat (1.5-3 s each), never the same shot twice in a row. Shots may be reused from earlier videos, but each video must feel entirely different.
HOW FOOTAGE MATCHES WORDS (like the best GTA Shorts): a line about a person shows that person (Jason, Lucia), a line about a place shows that place, an action shows that action. Abstract lines (prices, sizes, dates, percentages) are carried by a short on-screen 'callout' over striking, on-mood footage (Vice City, action, the leads) - that is correct here, not a mismatch.
FOR THE REVIEWERS: the game IS the topic, so Rockstar's official footage, characters and GTA V cover art are the approved pictures here (commentary on the game), not 'a brand or logo as the subject'.
FACTS: every number, date and claim comes from the sources; rumours and leaks are never stated as fact ('reportedly', 'Rockstar hasn't said'). Say WHO claims a thing ('fans spotted', 'PC Gamer reported') when Rockstar hasn't confirmed it. If no source gives a reason, say so plainly and make the payoff a surprising SOURCED FACT instead - never imply a link or reason the sources don't make. The TITLE must not assert anything unconfirmed (a question or 'fans say' is fine). No story spoilers beyond what Rockstar's trailers show. Never pretend the footage is our gameplay.
Say 'GTA 6' in beat 1 or 2 and in the title. No markers or arrows. Numbers go in 'callout' (short).
Length 30-38 seconds: 56-66 words, 10-12 beats of 4-7 words; beat 1 is at most 7 words (spoken prices count long: '$79.99' takes 2 s).
LOOP: the last line is a lead-in that flows back into beat 1; never 'So next time someone asks you'.
VERIFIED BRIEF: the angle below was researched and checked by Claude before writing (16 Nov 2026): use ITS facts, ITS cautious wording and ITS sources first; add nothing you cannot source.
LOOK AND FEEL: every video in this series must feel different - follow this video's own FORMAT (structure, pace, opening style) and choose FRESH shots; never copy another video's structure or opening.
SHOT-WORD MATCH: try hard to make every shot show what that line says (a person, place, object or action named in the line should be on screen). Search the SHOT LIST descriptions for the best match before settling.
PRE-FLIGHT CHECK - before you answer, test your own script against what the reviewers will check, and fix it first: (1) beat 1 is a question or shock in <=7 words over striking CLIP footage; (2) no line repeats an earlier line's point; (3) the payoff answers the hook with a SOURCED fact; (4) every claim Rockstar hasn't confirmed says who claims it; (5) each person/place/action line's shot shows that person/place/action (read the SHOT LIST description); (6) no shot is used in two beats in a row, and no 'avoid' shot is used; (7) 56-66 words; (8) the last line + beat 1 read as one sentence; (9) the title asserts nothing unconfirmed.

notes.format_rules:
GTA 6 SERIES RULES (owner, 16 Nov 2026 - these win over everything else):
STORY FIRST. The narrative is the most important thing. Structure: (1) HOOK in the first second - a surprising claim, a mystery or a 'wait, what?' moment, never a slow intro; (2) STAKES - why the viewer should care; (3) BUILD - 2-3 escalating reveals, each one more surprising; (4) PAYOFF - the satisfying answer or twist that makes people say 'wow'; (5) one short comment question people WANT to answer; (6) a last line that flows straight back into the first (loop). Every line must earn its place: no filler, no 'using official data'. 1-2 light witty lines. Speak like a friend telling a great story, not a news report.
FOOTAGE: every beat shows Rockstar's OFFICIAL GTA VI footage. In "images", each value is exactly 'CLIP:<shot_id>' from the SHOT LIST below (real trailer footage, full screen). Use 'OFFICIAL:<id>' (screenshot catalogue) only for GTA 5 (the cover v_c670974867, Los Santos v_24ba6644de / v_fdac18d437 / v_07edb091bb, the map v_3360902d78) or when no shot fits, and then ONLY for one short beat (max 2 s, 3-5 words). NEVER open on a still: beat 1 AND the last beat must be the same striking CLIP footage (the loop). No generated pictures. Pick the shot that matches what each line says. Beat 1 = the most striking, high-action or most beautiful shot that fits the hook. Use 8-11 different shots: a new shot every beat (1.5-3 s each), never the same shot twice in a row. Shots may be reused from earlier videos, but each video must feel entirely different.
HOW FOOTAGE MATCHES WORDS (like the best GTA Shorts): a line about a person shows that person (Jason, Lucia), a line about a place shows that place, an action shows that action. Abstract lines (prices, sizes, dates, percentages) are carried by a short on-screen 'callout' over striking, on-mood footage (Vice City, action, the leads) - that is correct here, not a mismatch.
FOR THE REVIEWERS: the game IS the topic, so Rockstar's official footage, characters and GTA V cover art are the approved pictures here (commentary on the game), not 'a brand or logo as the subject'.
FACTS: every number, date and claim comes from the sources; rumours and leaks are never stated as fact ('reportedly', 'Rockstar hasn't said'). Say WHO claims a thing ('fans spotted', 'PC Gamer reported') when Rockstar hasn't confirmed it. If no source gives a reason, say so plainly and make the payoff a surprising SOURCED FACT instead - never imply a link or reason the sources don't make. The TITLE must not assert anything unconfirmed (a question or 'fans say' is fine). No story spoilers beyond what Rockstar's trailers show. Never pretend the footage is our gameplay.
Say 'GTA 6' in beat 1 or 2 and in the title. No markers or arrows. Numbers go in 'callout' (short).
Length 30-38 seconds: 56-66 words, 10-12 beats of 4-7 words; beat 1 is at most 7 words (spoken prices count long: '$79.99' takes 2 s).
LOOP: the last line is a lead-in that flows back into beat 1; never 'So next time someone asks you'.
VERIFIED BRIEF: the angle below was researched and checked by Claude before writing (16 Nov 2026): use ITS facts, ITS cautious wording and ITS sources first; add nothing you cannot source.
LOOK AND FEEL: every video in this series must feel different - follow this video's own FORMAT (structure, pace, opening style) and choose FRESH shots; never copy another video's structure or opening.
SHOT-WORD MATCH: try hard to make every shot show what that line says (a person, place, object or action named in the line should be on screen). Search the SHOT LIST descriptions for the best match before settling.
PRE-FLIGHT CHECK - before you answer, test your own script against what the reviewers will check, and fix it first: (1) beat 1 is a question or shock in <=7 words over striking CLIP footage; (2) no line repeats an earlier line's point; (3) the payoff answers the hook with a SOURCED fact; (4) every claim Rockstar hasn't confirmed says who claims it; (5) each person/place/action line's shot shows that person/place/action (read the SHOT LIST description); (6) no shot is used in two beats in a row, and no 'avoid' shot is used; (7) 56-66 words; (8) the last line + beat 1 read as one sentence; (9) the title asserts nothing unconfirmed.

notes.question: Why GTA never uses real city names
notes.angle: HOOK: 'GTA 6 is set in Miami - so why won't Rockstar say Miami?' Vice City = Miami, Los Santos = Los Angeles, Liberty City = New York. Sourced reasons (creative freedom, legal/trademark caution, satire); label opinion. Payoff: fake names let them make fun of everything. CTA: 'Which real city should GTA do next?' FORMAT FOR THIS VIDEO (its own look and feel): MYSTERY: 'why won't Rockstar say Miami?' - clues, then the answer.
notes.format_rules:
GTA 6 SERIES RULES (owner, 16 Nov 2026 - these win over everything else):
STORY FIRST. The narrative is the most important thing. Structure: (1) HOOK in the first second - a surprising claim, a mystery or a 'wait, what?' moment, never a slow intro; (2) STAKES - why the viewer should care; (3) BUILD - 2-3 escalating reveals, each one more surprising; (4) PAYOFF - the satisfying answer or twist that makes people say 'wow'; (5) one short comment question people WANT to answer; (6) a last line that flows straight back into the first (loop). Every line must earn its place: no filler, no 'using official data'. 1-2 light witty lines. Speak like a friend telling a great story, not a news report.
FOOTAGE: every beat shows Rockstar's OFFICIAL GTA VI footage. In "images", each value is exactly 'CLIP:<shot_id>' from the SHOT LIST below (real trailer footage, full screen). Use 'OFFICIAL:<id>' (screenshot catalogue) only for GTA 5 (the cover v_c670974867, Los Santos v_24ba6644de / v_fdac18d437 / v_07edb091bb, the map v_3360902d78) or when no shot fits, and then ONLY for one short beat (max 2 s, 3-5 words). NEVER open on a still: beat 1 AND the last beat must be the same striking CLIP footage (the loop). No generated pictures. Pick the shot that matches what each line says. Beat 1 = the most striking, high-action or most beautiful shot that fits the hook. Use 8-11 different shots: a new shot every beat (1.5-3 s each), never the same shot twice in a row. Shots may be reused from earlier videos, but each video must feel entirely different.
HOW FOOTAGE MATCHES WORDS (like the best GTA Shorts): a line about a person shows that person (Jason, Lucia), a line about a place shows that place, an action shows that action. Abstract lines (prices, sizes, dates, percentages) are carried by a short on-screen 'callout' over striking, on-mood footage (Vice City, action, the leads) - that is correct here, not a mismatch.
FOR THE REVIEWERS: the game IS the topic, so Rockstar's official footage, characters and GTA V cover art are the approved pictures here (commentary on the game), not 'a brand or logo as the subject'.
FACTS: every number, date and claim comes from the sources; rumours and leaks are never stated as fact ('reportedly', 'Rockstar hasn't said'). Say WHO claims a thing ('fans spotted', 'PC Gamer reported') when Rockstar hasn't confirmed it. If no source gives a reason, say so plainly and make the payoff a surprising SOURCED FACT instead - never imply a link or reason the sources don't make. The TITLE must not assert anything unconfirmed (a question or 'fans say' is fine). No story spoilers beyond what Rockstar's trailers show. Never pretend the footage is our gameplay.
Say 'GTA 6' in beat 1 or 2 and in the title. No markers or arrows. Numbers go in 'callout' (short).
Length 30-38 seconds: 56-66 words, 10-12 beats of 4-7 words; beat 1 is at most 7 words (spoken prices count long: '$79.99' takes 2 s).
LOOP: the last line is a lead-in that flows back into beat 1; never 'So next time someone asks you'.
VERIFIED BRIEF: the angle below was researched and checked by Claude before writing (16 Nov 2026): use ITS facts, ITS cautious wording and ITS sources first; add nothing you cannot source.
LOOK AND FEEL: every video in this series must feel different - follow this video's own FORMAT (structure, pace, opening style) and choose FRESH shots; never copy another video's structure or opening.
SHOT-WORD MATCH: try hard to make every shot show what that line says (a person, place, object or action named in the line should be on screen). Search the SHOT LIST descriptions for the best match before settling.
PRE-FLIGHT CHECK - before you answer, test your own script against what the reviewers will check, and fix it first: (1) beat 1 is a question or shock in <=7 words over striking CLIP footage; (2) no line repeats an earlier line's point; (3) the payoff answers the hook with a SOURCED fact; (4) every claim Rockstar hasn't confirmed says who claims it; (5) each person/place/action line's shot shows that person/place/action (read the SHOT LIST description); (6) no shot is used in two beats in a row, and no 'avoid' shot is used; (7) 56-66 words; (8) the last line + beat 1 read as one sentence; (9) the title asserts nothing unconfirmed.

notes.angle: HOOK: 'GTA 5 made a billion dollars in three days. GTA 6 starts today.' Facts: GTA V $800M day one, $1B in 3 days (Guinness/Take-Two 2013); Take-Two said GTA 6 pre-orders are 'far in excess of our initial expectations' (9 Nov 2026). No predictions as fact. Payoff: what it needs to beat. CTA: 'Will GTA 6 beat it?' FORMAT FOR THIS VIDEO (its own look and feel): RECORD BATTLE: GTA 5's records vs GTA 6's start, scoreboard style.
notes.format_rules:
GTA 6 SERIES RULES (owner, 16 Nov 2026 - these win over everything else):
STORY FIRST. The narrative is the most important thing. Structure: (1) HOOK in the first second - a surprising claim, a mystery or a 'wait, what?' moment, never a slow intro; (2) STAKES - why the viewer should care; (3) BUILD - 2-3 escalating reveals, each one more surprising; (4) PAYOFF - the satisfying answer or twist that makes people say 'wow'; (5) one short comment question people WANT to answer; (6) a last line that flows straight back into the first (loop). Every line must earn its place: no filler, no 'using official data'. 1-2 light witty lines. Speak like a friend telling a great story, not a news report.
FOOTAGE: every beat shows Rockstar's OFFICIAL GTA VI footage. In "images", each value is exactly 'CLIP:<shot_id>' from the SHOT LIST below (real trailer footage, full screen). Use 'OFFICIAL:<id>' (screenshot catalogue) only for GTA 5 (the cover v_c670974867, Los Santos v_24ba6644de / v_fdac18d437 / v_07edb091bb, the map v_3360902d78) or when no shot fits, and then ONLY for one short beat (max 2 s, 3-5 words). NEVER open on a still: beat 1 AND the last beat must be the same striking CLIP footage (the loop). No generated pictures. Pick the shot that matches what each line says. Beat 1 = the most striking, high-action or most beautiful shot that fits the hook. Use 8-11 different shots: a new shot every beat (1.5-3 s each), never the same shot twice in a row. Shots may be reused from earlier videos, but each video must feel entirely different.
HOW FOOTAGE MATCHES WORDS (like the best GTA Shorts): a line about a person shows that person (Jason, Lucia), a line about a place shows that place, an action shows that action. Abstract lines (prices, sizes, dates, percentages) are carried by a short on-screen 'callout' over striking, on-mood footage (Vice City, action, the leads) - that is correct here, not a mismatch.
FOR THE REVIEWERS: the game IS the topic, so Rockstar's official footage, characters and GTA V cover art are the approved pictures here (commentary on the game), not 'a brand or logo as the subject'.
FACTS: every number, date and claim comes from the sources; rumours and leaks are never stated as fact ('reportedly', 'Rockstar hasn't said'). Say WHO claims a thing ('fans spotted', 'PC Gamer reported') when Rockstar hasn't confirmed it. If no source gives a reason, say so plainly and make the payoff a surprising SOURCED FACT instead - never imply a link or reason the sources don't make. The TITLE must not assert anything unconfirmed (a question or 'fans say' is fine). No story spoilers beyond what Rockstar's trailers show. Never pretend the footage is our gameplay.
Say 'GTA 6' in beat 1 or 2 and in the title. No markers or arrows. Numbers go in 'callout' (short).
Length 30-38 seconds: 56-66 words, 10-12 beats of 4-7 words; beat 1 is at most 7 words (spoken prices count long: '$79.99' takes 2 s).
LOOP: the last line is a lead-in that flows back into beat 1; never 'So next time someone asks you'.
VERIFIED BRIEF: the angle below was researched and checked by Claude before writing (16 Nov 2026): use ITS facts, ITS cautious wording and ITS sources first; add nothing you cannot source.
LOOK AND FEEL: every video in this series must feel different - follow this video's own FORMAT (structure, pace, opening style) and choose FRESH shots; never copy another video's structure or opening.
SHOT-WORD MATCH: try hard to make every shot show what that line says (a person, place, object or action named in the line should be on screen). Search the SHOT LIST descriptions for the best match before settling.
PRE-FLIGHT CHECK - before you answer, test your own script against what the reviewers will check, and fix it first: (1) beat 1 is a question or shock in <=7 words over striking CLIP footage; (2) no line repeats an earlier line's point; (3) the payoff answers the hook with a SOURCED fact; (4) every claim Rockstar hasn't confirmed says who claims it; (5) each person/place/action line's shot shows that person/place/action (read the SHOT LIST description); (6) no shot is used in two beats in a row, and no 'avoid' shot is used; (7) 56-66 words; (8) the last line + beat 1 read as one sentence; (9) the title asserts nothing unconfirmed.

notes.format_rules:
GTA 6 SERIES RULES (owner, 16 Nov 2026 - these win over everything else):
STORY FIRST. The narrative is the most important thing. Structure: (1) HOOK in the first second - a surprising claim, a mystery or a 'wait, what?' moment, never a slow intro; (2) STAKES - why the viewer should care; (3) BUILD - 2-3 escalating reveals, each one more surprising; (4) PAYOFF - the satisfying answer or twist that makes people say 'wow'; (5) one short comment question people WANT to answer; (6) a last line that flows straight back into the first (loop). Every line must earn its place: no filler, no 'using official data'. 1-2 light witty lines. Speak like a friend telling a great story, not a news report.
FOOTAGE: every beat shows Rockstar's OFFICIAL GTA VI footage. In "images", each value is exactly 'CLIP:<shot_id>' from the SHOT LIST below (real trailer footage, full screen). Use 'OFFICIAL:<id>' (screenshot catalogue) only for GTA 5 (the cover v_c670974867, Los Santos v_24ba6644de / v_fdac18d437 / v_07edb091bb, the map v_3360902d78) or when no shot fits, and then ONLY for one short beat (max 2 s, 3-5 words). NEVER open on a still: beat 1 AND the last beat must be the same striking CLIP footage (the loop). No generated pictures. Pick the shot that matches what each line says. Beat 1 = the most striking, high-action or most beautiful shot that fits the hook. Use 8-11 different shots: a new shot every beat (1.5-3 s each), never the same shot twice in a row. Shots may be reused from earlier videos, but each video must feel entirely different.
HOW FOOTAGE MATCHES WORDS (like the best GTA Shorts): a line about a person shows that person (Jason, Lucia), a line about a place shows that place, an action shows that action. Abstract lines (prices, sizes, dates, percentages) are carried by a short on-screen 'callout' over striking, on-mood footage (Vice City, action, the leads) - that is correct here, not a mismatch.
FOR THE REVIEWERS: the game IS the topic, so Rockstar's official footage, characters and GTA V cover art are the approved pictures here (commentary on the game), not 'a brand or logo as the subject'.
FACTS: every number, date and claim comes from the sources; rumours and leaks are never stated as fact ('reportedly', 'Rockstar hasn't said'). Say WHO claims a thing ('fans spotted', 'PC Gamer reported') when Rockstar hasn't confirmed it. If no source gives a reason, say so plainly and make the payoff a surprising SOURCED FACT instead - never imply a link or reason the sources don't make. The TITLE must not assert anything unconfirmed (a question or 'fans say' is fine). No story spoilers beyond what Rockstar's trailers show. Never pretend the footage is our gameplay.
Say 'GTA 6' in beat 1 or 2 and in the title. No markers or arrows. Numbers go in 'callout' (short).
Length 30-38 seconds: 56-66 words, 10-12 beats of 4-7 words; beat 1 is at most 7 words (spoken prices count long: '$79.99' takes 2 s).
LOOP: the last line is a lead-in that flows back into beat 1; never 'So next time someone asks you'.
VERIFIED BRIEF: the angle below was researched and checked by Claude before writing (16 Nov 2026): use ITS facts, ITS cautious wording and ITS sources first; add nothing you cannot source.
LOOK AND FEEL: every video in this series must feel different - follow this video's own FORMAT (structure, pace, opening style) and choose FRESH shots; never copy another video's structure or opening.
SHOT-WORD MATCH: try hard to make every shot show what that line says (a person, place, object or action named in the line should be on screen). Search the SHOT LIST descriptions for the best match before settling.
PRE-FLIGHT CHECK - before you answer, test your own script against what the reviewers will check, and fix it first: (1) beat 1 is a question or shock in <=7 words over striking CLIP footage; (2) no line repeats an earlier line's point; (3) the payoff answers the hook with a SOURCED fact; (4) every claim Rockstar hasn't confirmed says who claims it; (5) each person/place/action line's shot shows that person/place/action (read the SHOT LIST description); (6) no shot is used in two beats in a row, and no 'avoid' shot is used; (7) 56-66 words; (8) the last line + beat 1 read as one sentence; (9) the title asserts nothing unconfirmed.

notes.format_rules:
GTA 6 SERIES RULES (owner, 16 Nov 2026 - these win over everything else):
STORY FIRST. The narrative is the most important thing. Structure: (1) HOOK in the first second - a surprising claim, a mystery or a 'wait, what?' moment, never a slow intro; (2) STAKES - why the viewer should care; (3) BUILD - 2-3 escalating reveals, each one more surprising; (4) PAYOFF - the satisfying answer or twist that makes people say 'wow'; (5) one short comment question people WANT to answer; (6) a last line that flows straight back into the first (loop). Every line must earn its place: no filler, no 'using official data'. 1-2 light witty lines. Speak like a friend telling a great story, not a news report.
FOOTAGE: every beat shows Rockstar's OFFICIAL GTA VI footage. In "images", each value is exactly 'CLIP:<shot_id>' from the SHOT LIST below (real trailer footage, full screen). Use 'OFFICIAL:<id>' (screenshot catalogue) only for GTA 5 (the cover v_c670974867, Los Santos v_24ba6644de / v_fdac18d437 / v_07edb091bb, the map v_3360902d78) or when no shot fits, and then ONLY for one short beat (max 2 s, 3-5 words). NEVER open on a still: beat 1 AND the last beat must be the same striking CLIP footage (the loop). No generated pictures. Pick the shot that matches what each line says. Beat 1 = the most striking, high-action or most beautiful shot that fits the hook. Use 8-11 different shots: a new shot every beat (1.5-3 s each), never the same shot twice in a row. Shots may be reused from earlier videos, but each video must feel entirely different.
HOW FOOTAGE MATCHES WORDS (like the best GTA Shorts): a line about a person shows that person (Jason, Lucia), a line about a place shows that place, an action shows that action. Abstract lines (prices, sizes, dates, percentages) are carried by a short on-screen 'callout' over striking, on-mood footage (Vice City, action, the leads) - that is correct here, not a mismatch.
FOR THE REVIEWERS: the game IS the topic, so Rockstar's official footage, characters and GTA V cover art are the approved pictures here (commentary on the game), not 'a brand or logo as the subject'.
FACTS: every number, date and claim comes from the sources; rumours and leaks are never stated as fact ('reportedly', 'Rockstar hasn't said'). Say WHO claims a thing ('fans spotted', 'PC Gamer reported') when Rockstar hasn't confirmed it. If no source gives a reason, say so plainly and make the payoff a surprising SOURCED FACT instead - never imply a link or reason the sources don't make. The TITLE must not assert anything unconfirmed (a question or 'fans say' is fine). No story spoilers beyond what Rockstar's trailers show. Never pretend the footage is our gameplay.
Say 'GTA 6' in beat 1 or 2 and in the title. No markers or arrows. Numbers go in 'callout' (short).
Length 30-38 seconds: 56-66 words, 10-12 beats of 4-7 words; beat 1 is at most 7 words (spoken prices count long: '$79.99' takes 2 s).
LOOP: the last line is a lead-in that flows back into beat 1; never 'So next time someone asks you'.
VERIFIED BRIEF: the angle below was researched and checked by Claude before writing (16 Nov 2026): use ITS facts, ITS cautious wording and ITS sources first; add nothing you cannot source.
LOOK AND FEEL: every video in this series must feel different - follow this video's own FORMAT (structure, pace, opening style) and choose FRESH shots; never copy another video's structure or opening.
SHOT-WORD MATCH: try hard to make every shot show what that line says (a person, place, object or action named in the line should be on screen). Search the SHOT LIST descriptions for the best match before settling.
PRE-FLIGHT CHECK - before you answer, test your own script against what the reviewers will check, and fix it first: (1) beat 1 is a question or shock in <=7 words over striking CLIP footage; (2) no line repeats an earlier line's point; (3) the payoff answers the hook with a SOURCED fact; (4) every claim Rockstar hasn't confirmed says who claims it; (5) each person/place/action line's shot shows that person/place/action (read the SHOT LIST description); (6) no shot is used in two beats in a row, and no 'avoid' shot is used; (7) 56-66 words; (8) the last line + beat 1 read as one sentence; (9) the title asserts nothing unconfirmed.
